paper_title: Stronger limits on hypothetical Yukawa interactions in the 40--8000 nm range
notes: Casimir-less differential force measurement constraining Yukawa-type fifth force (alpha vs lambda) in the 30-8000 nm range, a test of non-Newtonian gravity / fifth force (ScalarNucleon-like). The result is presented in the {lambda, alpha} plane (Fig. 4) rather than in a coupling-vs-mass plane with numerical values, and no numerical table is provided. Mass would relate to lambda via m = hbar*c/lambda, but no extractable numerical (alpha, lambda) pairs are given in the text. Improvement up to factor 10^3 over previous limits at lambda=300 nm. 95% CL. | Vision: Figure 4 plots |alpha| (Yukawa strength relative to gravity) vs lambda in meters, not coupling vs mass in eV. The red curve is this work's limit (lower boundary of newly excluded region). X-values reported as mass in eV via m=hbar*c/lambda=1.973e-7/lambda[m]; lambda range 30 nm-100 um maps to ~6.5e-3 to ~2e1 eV (note: smaller lambda = larger mass). Y-axis is alpha (dimensionless Yukawa strength), mapped to ScalarNucleon coupling slot but is actually relative gravitational strength alpha, not a standard dimensionless coupling constant. Values approximate from log-log reading. | CV calibration unavailable (no plot region), used LLM axes | Calibration: No calibration needed | Auto-corrected couplings: ×1e-20 (×1.00e-20, rule=argmin|log10(median*f)-log10(anchor=1.0e-15)|)
